column1: # PB-SEC-8 -- the dependency inventory. "No analytics/telemetry SDKs; dependencies minimal
# EVERY MODULE THE BUILD RESOLVES, not the three the build file declares. The set is derived
# from android/gradle/verification-metadata.xml (PB-SEC-14's artifact), which enumerates what
# ACTUALLY resolves with a checksum for each -- so a transitive pull is as visible here as a
# declared one. An inventory read off `implementation` lines would report a clean bill of
# health for an app that ships the Google Play Services client stack.
# Regenerate after any dependency change, from android/:
# then rebuild this table and REVIEW THE DIFF. A new row is a new thing in the app.
# THREE CLASSES OF ROW, and the difference matters to a reviewer:
#   ships in the APK        -- on releaseRuntimeClasspath; runs on the user's handset.
#   test classpath only     -- on no variant runtime classpath; never packaged.
#   build classpath only    -- resolved to configure the build; runs on the build host, with
#                              full privileges on the machine that signs the release, which is
#                              why it is checksum-verified all the same.
# NO ANALYTICS, TELEMETRY, ATTRIBUTION OR CRASH-REPORTING MODULE IS PRESENT in any of the
# three. That is asserted, not claimed: android/gate/s18_sec8_depinventory_test.go matches a
# denylist against this same resolved closure. The absence of a crash reporter is deliberate
# and is recorded again in android/app/build.gradle.kts, because a reader who does not find it
# stated will eventually add one to "fix" the gap.
